title: Controlled Chaos in 4D SCFTs
authors: Florent Baume, Atakan Çavuşoğlu, Vivek Chakrabhavi, Jonathan J. Heckman
abstract: Chaotic dynamics play an important role in a number of physical systems. One of the qualitative hallmarks of this behavior is the appearance of a sufficiently "complex" spectrum of energy levels. This also makes it challenging to directly verify the onset of chaos in interacting quantum field theories. We present a class of 4D superconformal field theories (SCFTs) given by orbifolds of 4D $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang--Mills theory in which operator mixing in a controlled subsector is described by an effective spin chain in one spatial dimension with nearest neighbor interactions tuned by the marginal couplings of the SCFT. Tuning the marginal couplings results in a chaotic spectrum, while generically the spin chain exhibits Anderson localization. We diagnose the onset of chaos by analyzing the statistical distribution of eigenvalues of the dilatation operator, in particular properties such as eigenvalue level repulsion, spectral rigidity, and the spectral form factor. We also show that other diagnostics such as Krylov complexity sometimes do not faithfully capture this information. This structure defines a chaotic billiard in the target space of the stringy realization. We also comment on the large $N$ holographic dual description, where the controlled single spin chain approximation must be supplemented by multi-trace dynamics, i.e., the splitting and joining of multiple spin chains.
summary: The paper studies quantum chaos in 4D Superconformal Field Theories by mapping their operator mixing dynamics onto an effective spin chain model. By analyzing the energy spectrum's statistical properties—such as level repulsion and spectral rigidity—the authors demonstrate that tuning the SCFT couplings can drive the system into a chaotic regime, confirming theoretical predictions using random matrix theory diagnostics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how signatures of quantum chaos manifest within strongly coupled, higher-dimensional Quantum Field Theories (QFTs), specifically Superconformal Field Theories (SCFTs). It aims to diagnose the onset of chaos by analyzing spectral statistics.
main_result: The system exhibits chaotic spectral statistics when the coupling parameters ($b_i$) are tuned according to a specific power law distribution, confirming that quantum chaos can be diagnosed via random matrix ensemble signatures in these field theories.
method: Chaos is diagnosed by analyzing the statistical distribution of eigenvalues of the dilatation operator, focusing on metrics like eigenvalue level repulsion, spectral rigidity ($\Delta_3(E)$), and the spectral form factor. The dynamics are modeled using an effective spin chain Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system models a class of 4D SCFTs derived from orbifolds of $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang–Mills theory. The low-energy dynamics are effectively described by a nearest-neighbor interacting spin chain Hamiltonian governing operator mixing in a controlled subsector.
key_observables: Eigenvalue level repulsion, spectral rigidity ($\Delta_3(E)$), and the spectral form factor; Krylov complexity ($C_K(t)$).
important_parameters: The marginal couplings of the SCFT determine the hopping parameters $b_i$ in the spin chain. The analysis distinguishes between integrable regimes (e.g., all $b_i=b$), chaotic regimes, and intermediate Anderson localization.
main_assumptions: The analysis is primarily confined to one-loop mixing effects within the dilute gas approximation for the SCFT dynamics. Furthermore, the single spin chain approximation is noted to break down at large 't Hooft coupling, requiring multi-trace corrections.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares Krylov state complexity $C_K(t)$ evolution, showing distinct growth patterns for integrable versus chaotic regimes; Figure 1 shows level spacing ratios compared against theoretical predictions for various ensembles.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context by mapping SCFT dynamics onto a spin chain Hamiltonian. It then applies advanced diagnostics from quantum chaos theory (RMT statistics, complexity measures) to determine when the system transitions into a chaotic regime based on tuning the underlying couplings.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, calculable link between high-energy theoretical physics (SCFTs/AdS/CFT) and fundamental concepts from quantum chaos theory, using spectral statistics as the primary diagnostic tool.
